synthesizedFacts.fact: Exfoliation is a geological process where thin layers or sheets of rock are separated from the main rock body, often due to pressure release.
Exfoliation typically occurs in regions with moderate rainfall and is common in upland areas with exposures of uniform coarsely crystalline igneous rocks.
The process of exfoliation is not directly related to thermal expansion and contraction, as previously thought, but rather to pressure release and chemical weathering.
